items.title: Across the Horizon Ep. 75: Andrew Tuttle & Darren Cross
items.author: Flow State
items.content:
On today’s episode of Across the Horizon, Bob Holmes of the ambient country band SUSS has Andrew Tuttle & Darren Cross on the show to talk about their new release . Hailing from Australia, Andrew and Darren are experimental musicians whose banjo and acoustic guitar collaborations stretch the boundaries of ambient Americana. They also bring along a playlist of new instrumental music from their homeland including Lawrence English, Jordan Ireland, Monica Brooks, and more.

For Flow State we’re mostly off this week but today we’re listening to two Tuttle records, including . Tuttle (based in Brisbane) and Cross (in Sydney) play banjo and acoustic guitar / synth respectively, and both contribute to effects and mixing. The compositions are airy, the synths creating a big space for the banjo and guitar to resonate and linger. We’re also playing Tuttle’s 2022 record, , which foregrounds the banjo and features Cross on two tracks.

Have a great rest of your week.

items.title: Maryos Syawish
items.author: Flow State
items.content: It’s Friday so we’re listening to something slightly more upbeat. Today we’re listening to Maryos Syawish, an Iraqi electronic musician based in Naarm/Melbourne. He’s one half of the duo Sleep D, who we recommended back in 2020. His new record, , has been in the works for about eight years, mixing field recordings from his home country with synths and drum machines. Assummarized, there’s “meditative, shimmering atmospheres… stuttering, breakbeat-infected downtempo… wormhole-traversing electronics… and billowing, cinematic drone.” We’re also playing Sleep D’s 2019 LP, , which is more of a traditional Friday four-on-the-floor.

items.title: Time Wharp
items.author: Flow State
items.content: Today we’re listening to Time Wharp, an American multi-instrumentalist from Atlanta. The project is by Kaye Loggins, now based in Brooklyn. She played in bands in high school – punk, ska, metal, and “Myspace comedy techno” as she told Into. Terry Riley and the compilation pointed her towards ambient and experimental music. Her solo work as Time Wharp reflects her individual vision and unique collection of happenstance influences. Her album was released in 2022 on Leaving Records, manifesting the label’s “all-genre” ethos. There are elements of minimalism, jazz, leftfield electronic… First, though, we’re playing Radical American Hippy Kraut, whose “Blues 4 dANA” ended our neo-krautrock mix this week. It’s a collaboration with New York’s Charley Lanning aka CH Rom.
